string.name: wp_intro
string.value: This hands notification delivery to a server you run yourself. Enabling it means accepting the following trade-offs:

string.name: wp_warn_1
string.value: 1. Your server sees message previews in the clear. Decryption has to happen there — that is what this route requires, and it cannot be avoided.

string.name: wp_warn_2
string.value: 2. Previews may be partial or absent. Chats with previews turned off, and some message types, only push “You have a new message”.

string.name: wp_warn_3
string.value: 3. Delivery depends entirely on your server. If it goes down, its certificate expires or its address changes, nothing warns you and the app cannot tell.

string.name: wp_warn_4
string.value: 4. Only enter an address you control. Someone else's endpoint means handing them your message previews.

string.name: wp_warn_5
string.value: 5. This is an additional channel, not a replacement. The app's own background sync and local notifications keep working.

string.name: wp_enable_sub
string.value: A server you run receives Telegram's Web Push, decrypts it and forwards it to the channel of your choice.

string.name: wp_fill_three
string.value: Fill in the three fields below

string.name: wp_server_todo
string.value: What your server has to do

string.name: wp_server_steps
string.value:
1. Receive Telegram's POST requests at the endpoint.
2. Decrypt with your private key per RFC 8291 to get JSON containing loc_key / loc_args / custom.
3. Build the title and body from loc_key and forward them to your push channel.
4. Include tg://openmessage?channel_id=<custom.channel_id>&msg_id=<custom.msg_id> in the push so tapping the notification opens the chat directly (use from_id for private chats, chat_id for basic groups).

string.name: wp_keygen_note
string.value:
Generate a P-256 key pair and an auth secret on your server, keep the private key there, and fill in the three fields below. The app never holds the private key and takes no part in decryption.
In practice Telegram only delivers to https addresses with a domain name — http or a bare IP receives nothing.
